nomos-platform is Band 1p, the single platform port crate: its own lib.rs doc comment states the reason all its trait groups are bundled -- 'exactly one crate in the workspace names a platform dependency,' so swapping the implementation cannot recompile the bands above. Reviewed and answered already in commit baf823a4 ('Bind imports to the facade, and answer the four crate-split reviews'); splitting it now would undo that settled decision, not fix a defect.

nomos-platform-std is the std implementation of nomos-platform's unified port (Band 1p) and mirrors its bundled shape for the same reason -- a caller depending on the real implementation needs the whole port, not one trait's worth. Same baf823a4 review as nomos-platform.

nomos-spec-model's own lib.rs doc comment already answers this: the content model and the submission vocabulary are correctly read as two unreferencing groups today because the typed layer that would connect them (a submission naming the content it is about) does not exist yet. The comment states explicitly that splitting is a band-and-ownership decision this repository settles deliberately, not one to make while tidying the tree.

waivers.message: `Parse_Record(RECORD).expect("reads")` promises the compiler that this value is present, on your authority, and the reason it gives -- `reads` -- restates the problem rather than naming the invariant. The promise may well be true; what is missing is what MAKES it true. Name the invariant -- what has already validated this, and where -- so the next reader can check whether it still holds. A promise with a reason is an invariant; a promise without one is a bet, and the way you find out you lost it is a crash that explains nothing
